item.title: Matthew Stafford closing in on Philip Rivers for No. 6 on all-time passing TDs list
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford surpassed Dan Marino for No. 7 on the all-time passing touchdown list late last season.
item.content:encoded:
Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford surpassed Dan Marino for No. 7 on the all-time passing touchdown list late last season. Up next is Philip Rivers.

Stafford currently has 423 career touchdown passes, which puts him two behind Rivers, who threw for 425 touchdowns in his career.

If Stafford throws three touchdown passes on Thursday night against the 49ers, he'll have 426 in his career, and he'll be No. 6 on the all-time list.

Stafford has thrown 141 touchdown passes in five years with the Rams after throwing 282 touchdown passes in 12 years with the Lions. Rivers threw 397 touchdown passes in 16 years with the Chargers, then threw 24 more in 2020 with the Colts, then came out of retirement and threw four more touchdown passes in 2025 with the Colts. If Rivers hadn't come out of retirement last year, Stafford already would have surpassed his total.

The Top 5 in passing touchdowns in NFL history are Tom Brady with 649, Drew Brees with 571, Peyton Manning with 539, Aaron Rodgers with 527 and Brett Favre with 508.

item.content:encoded:
Running back TreVeyon Henderson will not be in the lineup for the Patriots in Seattle on Wednesday night.

Henderson has missed the last two weeks of practice with an ankle injury, so it came as no surprise that the Patriots officially ruled him out for their season opener on Tuesday. The Patriots previously announced that offensive lineman Ben Brown will miss the game with a knee injury and no other players have injury designations.

Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are the other running backs on the 53-man roster for New England. Hassan Haskins and Lan Larison are available to be elevated from the practice squad.

item.title: Bucs announce three-year extension with Baker Mayfield
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The third deal the QB has signed with the Bucs will keep him under contract with the team through the 2029 season.
item.content:encoded:
A deal that looked like it might not get done got done Tuesday.

The Buccaneers announced Baker Mayfield's three-year extension, which reportedly will pay him $165 million and keep him under contract with the team through the 2029 season.

"Baker's arrival marked an important new chapter for our organization, and over the past three years he has established himself as the unquestioned leader of our franchise" Buccaneers owner Joel Glazer said in a statement. "This contract — the largest in the history of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers — reflects our belief in Baker, and his leadership both on and off the field. His competitive spirit, resilience and commitment to winning embody everything we want in our players. Baker and his wife, Emily, have made a meaningful impact in the Tampa Bay community and we are thrilled their family will continue to call Tampa Bay home for years to come."

After Mayfield's imposed deadline passed without receiving a new contract at the start of training camp, the quarterback said he felt disrespected and undervalued. The sides continued to talk, though, leading to Tuesday's outcome.

It is the third contract Mayfield has signed with the Bucs, following a one-year, $4 million, prove-it deal in 2023 and a three-year, $100 million extension a year later.

In his first three seasons as the Buccaneers' starting quarterback, Mayfield ranks second in the NFL in touchdown passes (95) and third in passing yards (12,237) and has led the team to a pair of division championships.

"Baker is the ultimate competitor, and the guys in our locker room feed off the energy, confidence and toughness he brings every day," coach Todd Bowles said in a statement. "He prepares the right way, holds himself accountable and is an unquestioned leader for our team. His belief in himself and this team never wavers, and he sets the tone for us every day. That is what you want from the person leading your football team, and we are excited to continue building with him as our quarterback."

Mayfield was set to enter the final year of that contract in 2026.

item.title: Nick Bosa hopes to play with "no reservations" against Rams
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The 49ers have already revealed that defensive end Nick Bosa will be playing against the Rams on Thursday, which means the biggest question left about his return to action after last year's torn ACL is how much he'll be on the field.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have already revealed that defensive end Nick Bosa will be playing against the Rams on Thursday, which means the biggest question left about his return to action after last year's torn ACL is how much he'll be on the field.

Bosa has his eyes on a full workload. He said he "couldn't be happier with where I'm at" after ramping up at practice over the last week and feels well enough that he'd tell defensive line coach Kris Kocurek that he wants to play without any limitations.

"I haven't talked to Kris yet, but I'm going to hope for no reservations," Bosa said, via NBCSportsBayArea.com. "But we'll see what he says."

49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said at his press conference that the team will have to "be smart" with both Bosa and tight end George Kittle in their return from long layoffs, so Bosa may not get exactly what he wants as the team welcomes him back to the lineup.

item.title: Seahawks pick different captains for each game, including Sam Darnold for Week 1
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Seahawks open the season on Wednesday night against the Patriots, quarterback Sam Darnold will be one of their captains.
item.content:encoded:
When the Seahawks open the season on Wednesday night against the Patriots, quarterback Sam Darnold will be one of their captains. But that won't be the case every week.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald believes in picking new captains for each game, rather than the season-long captains with a 'C' on their jersey that most teams use. That was Macdonald's approach during his first two seasons as the Seahawks' head coach, and it will continue to be his approach this year.

In addition to Darnold, the Seahawks' captains against the Patriots will be linebacker Ernest Jones IV, fullback Brady Russell and defensive tackle Leonard Williams.

Macdonald said early in the 2024 season, his first as a head coach, that he believes in making team captain a weekly recognition rather than a season-long responsibility.

“It’s a combination of guys who are doing a great job, guys who are trying to build up and give an opportunity to have a voice with the rest of the team, guys you want to recognize that deserve an opportunity to do those things," Macdonald said. "So, that’s really the thought behind it. It’s pretty much that simple. The guys know who the leaders are. You don’t need the title to be the leader of the team. But it’s important to build everybody else up. . . . There’s nothing formal about it. It’s just more of a recognition type thing. Just, ‘Hey, shout out to these guys that are operating the right way, playing the right way, preparing the right way.’"

As the starting quarterback, Darnold was an obvious choice for Week 1. He'll be a team leader all year, and doesn't need the captain's 'C' to show it.

item.title: Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori remains limited, S Ty Okada DNP again on Monday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori remained limited in Monday's practice.
item.content:encoded:
Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori remained limited in Monday's practice. That doesn't bode well for his availability for Wednesday's season opener against the Patriots.

Emmanwori did not take participate in any of the team’s open practices during camp, according to Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times. Emmanwori is working his way back from arthroscopic surgery in July to repair his right ankle, which he initially injured in the 2025 season opener and then aggravated in a practice before Super Bowl LX.

Starting safety Ty Okada's status for Week 1 also is in question as he missed a second consecutive day. The team's other starting safety, Julian Neal, was a full participant a second consecutive day with a quad injury.

D’Anthony Bell, who re-signed to the practice squad on Saturday, started two games in Emmanwori’s third safety role a year ago when Emmanwori was out with an ankle injury.

The Seahawks had only one change to their practice report from Sunday, with offensive guard Anthony Bradford (knee) upgraded to full participation. Bradford was limited on Sunday.

Wide receiver Tory Horton (hamstring) and offensive tackle Josh Jones (knee) again were limited.

Tight end A.J. Barner (oblique) and running back Emanuel Wilson (hamstring) remained full participants.

item.title: NFL stops Vikings from signing Kenny Dyson to practice squad after he was waived-injured
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: At the end of the preseason, the Vikings waived outside linebacker Kenny Dyson with an injury settlement.
item.content:encoded:
At the end of the preseason, the Vikings waived outside linebacker Kenny Dyson with an injury settlement. A week later, the Vikings attempted to sign Dyson to their practice squad. The league said no.

Dyson's practice squad contract was disallowed because of a league rule that say players waived with an injury settlement can't be re-signed by that team until the length of the injury settlement, plus three weeks.

In other words, if Dyson's injury settlement (which has not been publicly revealed) was four weeks' salary, that means the Vikings wouldn't be allowed to bring him back until at least seven weeks into the season. Dyson is free to sign with another team before then, just not the Vikings.

Injury settlements can be beneficial to both the team and the player: For the team, reaching an injury settlement with the player prevents them from having to put him on injured reserve, so he can play for them later in the season once he's healthy. For the player, accepting the settlement allows him to take that money but still potentially play later in the season.

Dyson may still play this season. He could sign with another team at any time in the next seven weeks, or he could sign with the Vikings, once he becomes eligible to do so.

item.title: Denzel Ward purchases a stake in the Cleveland Guardians
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Browns cornerback Denzel Ward signed a two-year contract extension this offseason and he's investing some of that money in another one of the city's sports teams.
item.content:encoded:
Browns cornerback Denzel Ward signed a two-year contract extension this offseason and he's investing some of that money in another one of the city's sports teams.

According to multiple reports, Ward has purchased a stake in the Cleveland Guardians. The Guardians are owned by Paul Dolan and David Blitzer with Blitzer in position to become the team's majority owner in the coming years.

Ward is not the only NFL player with a stake in the Guardians. Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce is also a minority shareholder in the club and both players attended this year's home opener in Blitzer's suite.

Ward grew up outside of Cleveland and has spent his entire NFL career with the Browns. The investment in the Guardians suggests he'll remain tied to the city beyond his playing career as well.

item.title: Report: Broncos owners intend to secure control of MLB's Rockies
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Broncos owners Carrie Walton Penner and Greg Penner currently hold 40 percent of the MLB's Colorado Rockies.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos owners Carrie Walton Penner and Greg Penner currently hold 40 percent of the MLB's Colorado Rockies. Whenever baseball's looming labor mess ends, they're expected to emerge with controlling interest in the local baseball franchise

Via Woody Paige of the Colorado Springs Gazette, the Penners intend to acquire another 35 percent of the Rockies once the baseball Collective Bargaining Agreement is resolved.

The Walton-Penner group bought the Broncos in 2022 for a then-record $4.65 billion, less than half the recent price paid for the Seahawks.

Their fortune traces to the Walmart empire, which has spawned a cluster of multibillionaires. The Broncos' ownership group instantly became the richest in the NFL, by far, and they're willing to spend their money for the betterment of the team — which gives them a real advantage over their competitors.

Last year, in their fourth season of ownership, the Broncos won the No. 1 seed in the AFC and nearly secured a Super Bowl berth, The team is one of the short-list favorites for 2026.

item.content:encoded:
Another year, another opportunity to make a variety of grossly inaccurate prognostications about the NFL season to come.

When guessing right, it's regarded as the product of dumb luck. When guessing wrong, it serves as confirmation that the person making the predictions was and is an idiot.

But, hey, when in Rome. And the job compels us to give it a shot, whatever the outcome may be. The 2026 playoff trees and Super Bowl champions for each of the PFT writers appear below.

Fortunately, the results aren't part of our annual performance reviews. If they were, we'd all be fired. Starting with me, even though I own the place.

item.title: PFT's Week 1 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The defending champs still cling to the top spot, barely.
item.content:encoded:
1. Seahawks (preseason No. 1; 0-0): Is rookie Jadarian Price ready to carry the load in the running game?

2. Rams (No. 2; 0-0): Anything short of a Super Bowl appearance will be viewed as failure.

3. Texans (No. 3; 0-0): If the offense is just a little bit better, they could be a Super Bowl team.

4. Broncos (No. 4; 0-0): Jaylen Waddle could be just what the passing game needed.

5. Bills (No. 5; 0-0): How many grass fields does it take to finish a football season? (We're about to find out.)

6. Bears (No. 6; 0-0): Forty-one years after the pinnacle of the 46 defense, can they do enough on that side of the ball?

7. Patriots (No. 7; 0-0): The first four games are a meat grinder, especially in comparison to last year's cakewalk.

8. Eagles (No. 8; 0-0): Sean Mannion has the chance to be the next one-and-done offensive coordinator — either because he gets promoted or because he gets replaced.

9. Jaguars (No. 9; 0-0): In Year 2 of the Liam Coen/Trevor Lawrence marriage, the sky is the limit.

10. Ravens (No. 10; 0-0): Lamar Jackson is very excited about the new offense, which should have Ravens fans feeling very good about the team's prospects.

11. Bengals (No. 15; 0-0): Joe Burrow thinks it feels like LSU circa 2019. We'll defer to his expertise, for now.

12. Chargers (No. 11; 0-0): The clock is ticking on Justin Herbert fulfilling his full potential.

13. Chiefs (No. 13; 0-0): When it's time to call the plays, will they truly commit to the run?

14. Lions (No. 14; 0-0): Falling into a fourth-place schedule gives them the inside track to winning the division.

15. 49ers (No. 12; 0-0): It's impossible to ignore the collective impact of one weird story after another.

16. Packers (No. 16; 0-0): Losing Josh Jacobs to paid leave could be a big problem, especially with Micah Parsons still not ready to go.

17. Cowboys (No. 17; 0-0): The offensive line is suddenly a question mark.

18. Steelers (No. 18; 0-0): They need to get off to a fast start; there are plenty of tough games after the Week 9 bye.

19. Vikings (No. 20; 0-0): If the offense clicks under Kyler Murray, they could be one of the most balanced teams in the league.

20. Giants (No. 23; 0-0): John Harbaugh may have them on the brink of a quick turnaround.

21. Panthers (No. 19; 0-0): Can Bryce Young secure his future in Carolina?

22. Buccaneers (No. 21; 0-0): They need another fast start — and not another collapse thereafter.

23. Colts (No. 22; 0-0): They desperately need Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor to stay healthy.

24. Saints (No. 24; 0-0): If they'd started Tyler Shough from Week 1 of last year, they may have won the division.

25. Falcons (No. 25; 0-0): If/when Tua gets benched, he could soon end up being cut.

26. Titans (No. 27; 0-0): Robert Saleh gets an immediate chance to act on the grudge he claims he doesn't hold against the Jets.

27. Commanders (No. 26; 0-0): It already feels like it's just a matter of time before Dan Quinn is relieved of his duties.

28. Dolphins (No. 28; 0-0): The right culture is in place. Do they have the right players?

29. Jets (No. 29; 0-0): Jets fans find plenty of optimism in 0-0. They should enjoy it while it lasts.

30. Raiders (No. 31; 0-0): How long until Maxx Crosby is traded?

31. Browns (No. 30; 0-0): Deshaun Watson's two-game audition likely won't be good enough to get him to Week 3.

32. Cardinals (No. 32; 0-0): Beyond the question of whether Jeremiyah Love can get healthy is the question of whether the Cardinals can keep him healthy.

item.title: Aaron Glenn: We'll make the right decision at kicker when it needs to be done
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets are set at most of the key spots in their lineup heading into Sunday's opener against the Titans, but there's one position that's still up in the air.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets are set at most of the key spots in their lineup heading into Sunday's opener against the Titans, but there's one position that's still up in the air.

Kicker Blake Grupe was claimed off of waivers last week, which led to Jason Sanders being released from the active roster. Sanders returned to the practice squad, however, and head coach Aaron Glenn said on Tuesday that he has not made a call about who will handle the role in Nashville.

Glenn said the team will "make the right decision when that decision needs to be done."

"I said it before, I'm not going to panic about that situation," Glenn said, via the team's website. "I think they're both capable men, all right. And at the end of the day, we got to pick one guy that's going to be a kicker."

The overall arc of the Jets' season will likely be more reliant on other positions, but the wrong choice at kicker could cost the team chances to win games and that makes it a big choice for Glenn to make as he tries to improve on a disappointing first season at the helm.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants released longtime starting wideout Darius Slayton this week and they released a depth chart showing who is now on the first team on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants released longtime starting wideout Darius Slayton this week and they released a depth chart showing who is now on the first team on Tuesday.

Malik Nabers fills one of the spots and Darnell Mooney is listed next to him as the other starter. While many teams also list a third wideout or slot receiver among their starters, the Giants only went with a pair of wideouts on the first string.

Mooney signed with the Giants as a free agent this offseason and is listed ahead of Odell Beckham. Rookie Malachi Fields is behind Nabers and the Giants do not have any other receivers on their 53-man roster at present.

Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones are among the wideouts on the practice squad and are listed on the depth chart as returners, so that group could grow once the Giants finalize their roster for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: I thought Aaron Donald would play, never been more excited to be wrong
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "I was preparing for the worst, and glad we don't have to see him this week," Shanahan said.
item.content:encoded:
Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald will not play against the 49ers on Thursday night, which was a pleasant surprise to 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan.

Shortly after the Rams announced that Donald will not travel to Australia for the game against the 49ers, Shanahan described himself as "very excited," telling reporters he was fully expecting to have to go against the three-time Defensive Player of the Year.

"I told you guys last time I talked to you he was definitely playing," Shanahan said. "I've never been more excited to be wrong about something."

Shanahan is glad the 49ers won't have to play against Donald until their second game against the Rams, in December.

"We're going to have to see him eventually, we play them twice, but I was hoping he wouldn't," Shanahan said. "I was preparing for the worst, and glad we don't have to see him this week."

item.title: Aaron Rodgers: Steelers are Super Bowl contenders, that's why I came back
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: "I like the roster as a whole," Rodgers said. "We have good veteran leadership. It's just about going out there and doing it."
item.content:encoded:
Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers has no doubt that he can end his career by winning a Super Bowl.

Asked by Adam Schein if the Steelers are among the teams that are realistic contenders to win the Super Bowl, Rodgers didn't hesitate.

"Yeah, of course. Of course. That's why I came back, because I believe in the guys," Rodgers said.

Rodgers then rattled off the names of several teammates he's expecting to have good seasons, on offense, defense and special teams, and said he believes the Steelers have built a team that can compete with anyone.

"I like the roster as a whole," Rodgers said. "We have good veteran leadership. It's just about going out there and doing it. I feel like the AFC is very deep. Even our own division has a number of teams with Super Bowl aspirations, which is great."

Rodgers has said this will be his final NFL season. Five months from now, he believes it's realistic to think he'll ride off into the sunset with the Lombardi Trophy in his hands.

item.title: 49ers DT Alfred Collins out for season with knee injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: 49ers defensive tackle Alfred Collins tore his patellar tendon in practice this week, according to coach Kyle Shanahan.
item.content:encoded:
49ers defensive tackle Alfred Collins tore his patellar tendon in practice this week, according to coach Kyle Shanahan. Collins is out for the season.

The 49ers had listed Collins as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice. (The 49ers are in Australia, so it was Wednesday in Australia.)

The 49ers have Osa Odighizuwa, CJ West, Gracen Halton and James Thompson Jr. left at the position. In the first official practice of the week, Thompson missed practice with a hamstring injury, and Halton was limited with an ankle injury.

It seems likely the 49ers will call up one of their practice squad defensive tackles — Sebastian Valdez or Kevin Givens — for the game.

Collins, a second-round pick in 2025, played 16 games last season and totaled 17 tackles, one sack, four quarterback hits, an interception, two passes defensed and two forced fumbles.

The 49ers have spent the week in Melbourne as they prepare for Thursday's season opener against the Rams.

item.title: LSU finalizes roster, preventing the addition of two former NFL players
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: LSU is apparently throwing in the towel in its fight to add two fifth-year players who signed NFL teams from joining the Tigers football team.
item.content:encoded:
LSU is apparently throwing in the towel in its fight to add two fifth-year players who signed NFL teams from joining the Tigers football team.

According to multiple reports, LSU added two players to the school's roster. The addition of Aiden Anding and Gabriel Reliford fills the school's 105-player roster.

It comes days after a Baton Rouge judge granted eligibility to Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. Wright signed with the Eagles as an undrafted free agent, joined the Browns after being waived by Philadelphia and then was cut by Cleveland. Harris signed with the Saints as an undrafted free agent before the team waived him.

Louisiana plaintiffs' attorney Ryan Downton said Wright and Harris are reviewing legal options.

It is not yet known whether the SEC will cancel a potential vote Thursday to expel LSU from the conference, which would require 11 schools in favor.

item.title: Report: Steelers made an offer to Joey Porter Jr., but sides aren't close
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Christian Gonzalez agreed to a four-year, $135 million extension with the Patriots, providing a template for a Porter deal.
item.content:encoded:
Christian Gonzalez agreed to a four-year, $135 million contract with the Patriots early Tuesday morning, leaving Joey Porter Jr. as the last big-name cornerback waiting for a long-term deal.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Media reports that the Steelers made an offer to Porter, but that the proposed deal was "not good enough . . . to be deemed close."

The sides are at least negotiating with time running out.

The Steelers do not negotiate contract extensions once the season starts.

Porter spent training camp on the active/physically unable to perform list with what the team called a back issue. He returned to practice last Tuesday, and the Steelers began contract talks thereafter.

He has been noncommittal about playing Week 1 absent a contract extension.

Porter will need to ramp up to get on the field for the season opener against the Falcons, but coach Mike McCarthy said Monday he was "hopeful" that Porter will be in the lineup.

Seattle cornerback Devon Witherspoon signed a four-year, $132 million extension on Aug. 15, so the Steelers will likely have to top both Witherspoon and Gonzalez for Porter to agree to a long-term deal.

item.title: Myles Garrett ready for start of season despite lack of training camp reps
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett did not practice Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Rams outside linebacker Myles Garrett did not practice Tuesday. He has not practiced much this summer, missing most of training camp with knee swelling.

He did return to practice Sunday and also practiced Monday, and coach Sean McVay said Garrett will play in the season opener against the Rams on Thursday.

It seems likely that Garrett is on a snap count, but no one is saying.

Garrett didn't answer how he felt physically, stating simply that he's ready for the season opener despite the lack of training camp reps.

“I think I’ll be able to play off of some great teammates,” Garrett said, via Benjamin Royer of ocregister.com. “We have a strong defense all around, and they’ll make it easy, even if I am a touch off of what I usually am. I don’t suspect that I will be, but I have plenty of support, that’s all I’m saying.”

Garrett set the NFL record with 23 sacks last season, winning his second Defensive Player of the Year award. But late last season, that's all he and the Browns had to play for.

It was that way for most of his career in Cleveland, with the Browns going 58-90 with two playoff appearances in Garrett's nine seasons there. The Rams' aspirations are much higher.

“Super Bowl,” Garrett said. “Win DPOY again, obviously. I think those are the two main things on my mind, and going out and just being the best player I can be. I think there is a whole bunch of opportunities out there for, for us as the D-line to be something truly special, and I just want us to be able to realize that and, and never go into the locker room after a game feeling like we could’ve achieved more or done more.”

item.title: Nick Bosa, George Kittle limited participants in practice
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The 49ers released their first practice report of 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers released their first practice report of 2026.

The team, which has been in Australia for the past five days, lists nine players as limited during Tuesday's practice. Defensive end Nick Bosa (knee) and tight end George Kittle (Achilles) are among that group.

49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said a day earlier that Bosa will play, but it is unclear how much Bosa will play.

Bosa tore the ACL in his right knee in a Sept. 21 game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery Sept. 26. As he was coming back this summer, Bosa experienced soreness and tendinitis, and the 49ers backed him down until Sept. 2 when he returned to practice.

Kittle's status sounds a little more up in the air, with offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak offering only Kittle is in "good shape" to play.

Kittle tore his right Achilles in a Jan. 11 playoff game against the Eagles. He underwent surgery three days later, with Rams team physician Dr. Neal ElAttrache repairing Kittle’s Achilles.

Like Bosa, if Kittle plays, he likely is on a snap count.

Defensive tackle Alfred Collins (knee), linebacker Luke Gifford (hamstring), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (Achilles), defensive tackle Gracen Halton (ankle), defensive end Romello Height (ankle) and fullback Kyle Juszczyk (finger) also were limited.

Defensive tackle James Thompson (hamstring) did not practice, and cornerback Upton Stout (Achilles) was a full participant.

item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Pass rusher Myles Garrett has not practiced much this summer because of knee swelling, and he did not practice Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Pass rusher Myles Garrett has not practiced much this summer because of knee swelling, and he did not practice Tuesday.

The reigning Defensive Player of the Year will play in Thursday's season opener in Australia, head coach Sean McVay said. It will mark Garrett's debut with the Rams, who traded for him in June.

Garrett returned to practice Sunday and also participated on Monday, but the Rams did not have to release their first practice report of 2026 until Tuesday. And Garrett did not do any work with teammates before the team's departure for Melbourne on Tuesday night.

Defensive lineman Aaron Donald, who will not make the trip, had limited work on Tuesday as he works his way back into playing shape. Donald has not played an NFL game since 2023.

Tight end Tyler Higbee (rest), offensive tackle Alaric Jackson (rest), cornerback Jaylen Watson (toe) and linebacker Byron Young (rest) did not participate.

Linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring) was limited.

item.title: Dolphins LT Patrick Paul: Maxx Crosby is a hothead, have to get him off his game
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When the Dolphins hosted the Raiders in 2024, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby helped set up an early Miami touchdown by drawing an unnecessary roughness penalty for taking a swipe at Dolphins guard Liam Eichenberg.
item.content:encoded:
When the Dolphins hosted the Raiders in 2024, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby helped set up an early Miami touchdown by drawing an unnecessary roughness penalty for taking a swipe at Dolphins guard Liam Eichenberg.

After the Dolphins win, Eichenberg — who is currently out of the NFL — said that Crosby is "easy to aggravate" and one of his former teammates on the offensive line might be trying to do just that ahead of this Sunday's game.

Dolphins left tackle Patrick Paul said at a Tuesday press conference that one of the keys to dealing with the Raiders star is "getting him off his game" and he was asked about the role trash talk can play in that process.

“I feel like, yeah, he’s a hothead," Paul said, via David Furones of the South Florida Sun-Sentinel. "A lot of those things you could get into his game with that, but, I mean, he’s a great player so you just gotta stay on it all four quarters.”

Given Crosby's penchant for making life miserable for opposing quarterbacks, anything Paul can do to keep Crosby off of Malik Willis will be appreciated by the Dolphins this weekend.

item.title: Steelers first-rounder Max Iheanachor's house was burglarized last month
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Another NFL player's house has been burglarized.
item.content:encoded:
Another NFL player's house has been burglarized.

Via Jenna Harner of WPXI-TV, thieves targeted the home of Steelers 2026 first-round tackle Max Iheanachor on Wednesday, August 26. That day, the Steelers traveled to Buffalo for a preseason game on Thursday, August 27.

Per the report, the criminals absconded with $157,000 worth of jewelry, Rolexes, and designer bags.

No suspects have been identified.

It's the latest example of the fact that the travel habits of pro athletes are well known, to anyone and to everyone who may be inclined to wreak havoc. It's an unavoidable reality of the industry, and it puts an even greater premium on having appropriate security measures in place.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Defensive tackle Aaron Donald won't be in the Rams' lineup when they take the field against the 49ers in Melbourne, Australia this week, but defensive end Myles Garrett will be on hand.
item.content:encoded:
Defensive tackle Aaron Donald won't be in the Rams' lineup when they take the field against the 49ers in Melbourne, Australia this week, but defensive end Myles Garrett will be on hand.

After head coach Sean McVay announced that Donald will not travel with the team for the season opener, he confirmed that Garrett is "ready to go" for his Rams debut. Garrett returned to practice on Sunday after missing time with a knee injury.

"He's looked great," McVay said, via the team's website. "We've been smart with Myles, like I've kind of told you guys, but his impact has been tremendous, his overall vibe, what kind of teammate he's been. And so looking forward to getting him out there with the guys and being a great factor for us."

The Rams will have to wait at least another week to see what the Donald/Garrett duo looks like, but they'll get their first chance to experience life with Garrett in a couple of days.

item.title: in 2017, John Harbaugh wanted Colin Kaepernick in Baltimore
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: With former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick on the brink of releasing a new book, he's been talking a little more than usual as part of the promotion.
item.content:encoded:
With former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick on the brink of releasing a new book, he's been talking a little more than usual as part of the promotion. That has prompted others to have a few things to say, too.

One voice was somewhat unexpected. Giants coach John Harbaugh has spoken at length to Ian O'Connor of The Athletic regarding the Ravens' interest in Kaepernick after he became a free agent in 2017.

With Kaepernick's former 49ers coach, Jim Harbaugh, coaching at Michigan — and believing that a team could win "championships" with Kaepernick, John Harbaugh was very intrigued.

John Harbaugh also vividly remembered what happened in Super Bowl XLVII, when Baltimore barely held off a Kaepernick-led second-half comeback attempt.

“In that Super Bowl, he was really a nightmare to defend," John Harbaugh told O'Connor.

The biggest complication at the time related to Kaepernick's weekly protests in 2016, which sparked a broader wave of players taking a stand by not standing during the national anthem. And a significant public backlash from a sizable chunk of NFL fans.

“In all honesty, that wasn’t a factor,” John Harbaugh told O'Connor. “Yeah, there was conversation that there’s going to be a certain percentage of the fanbase that’s not going to appreciate this, but we decided that wasn’t going to be our driving factor.”

For the Ravens, who still had Super Bowl XLVII MVP Joe Flacco under contract, the attraction to Kaepernick was undeniable.

“His talent, and also the fact I had inside information as to who he was from my brother,” John Harbaugh told O'Connor. “We talked a lot about him, and I’d met Kap many times, had numerous conversations with him because of that. We talked about it at length as an organization, and we liked the fit. . . . The bottom line is your quarterback has to make plays for you, and Colin Kaepernick proved he could do that.”

The potential signing of Kaepernick became derailed for reasons that still remain fuzzy. His girlfriend, Nessa Diab, posted an image of franchise legend Ray Lewis and team owner Steve Bisciotti, after reports emerged that Bisciotti resisted the notion of embracing Kaepernick. After that, the visit never happened.

Even if Kaepernick's visit to Baltimore had happened, there would have been complications. Flacco was the starter. Kaepernick would have been the backup, with a contract reflecting his status. At the time, Kaepernick believed he should still be a starter; would he have accepted a secondary role?

If Kaepernick and the Ravens had joined forces, the ensuing butterfly effect could have resulted in the Ravens not trading back into the bottom of round one to acquire two-time MVP Lamar Jackson in April 2018. On that topic, Harbaugh said "we probably would’ve still drafted Lamar for the opportunity to have two guys like that."

Still, no one knows what would have happened without knowing how Kaepernick would have performed. In 2017, the Ravens went 9-7 and missed the playoffs; Flacco was so-so. If Kaepernick had gotten a chance to play that year and if he had played well, who knows? He could have been the clear-cut No. 1 entering 2018, perhaps making them less inclined to draft Jackson.

item.title: Joe Burrow: I'm here for the long haul; I'm not going anywhere
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Carson Palmer forced his way out of Cincinnati in 2011, requesting a trade and threatening to retire rather than play for the Bengals again.
item.content:encoded:
Carson Palmer forced his way out of Cincinnati in 2011, requesting a trade and threatening to retire rather than play for the Bengals again. At the 2011 trade deadline, the Bengals sent the quarterback to the Raiders.

Some have surmised that Joe Burrow's time with the team could see a similar exit after the current Bengals quarterback has, at times, expressed frustration with the organization.

He recently made a "now or never" declaration for the 2026 season, again inviting speculation about his future in Cincinnati. Burrow clarified in an exclusive interview with Geoff Hobson of the team website that it was not meant as an ultimatum.

"I'm efficient with my words, and when I'm efficient with my words, that leaves some room for interpretation," Burrow said. "But I mean what I say. I’m here for the long haul. I'm not going anywhere. I'm just trying to bring a now-or-never mentality to the day-by-day process. If you're not, what are you doing? Attack the day with a championship mindset. The rest will take care of itself."

After reaching Super Bowl LVI in 2021 and the AFC Championship Game in 2022, the Bengals have missed the postseason in each of the past three years.

The franchise has never won a Super Bowl, and Burrow wants to change.

Burrow grew up in Ohio, graduated from high school in Ohio and began his college career at Ohio State. Playing for the Bengals means more to him than Palmer, a California native, or perhaps any other quarterback to play in Cincinnati.

"I'm just really proud to be quarterback of the Bengals," Burrow said. "I'm happy to be here. I'm proud to represent the city of Cincinnati, state of Ohio, the Brown family. I'm just proud and I want to make everybody else proud, too."

item.title: Raiders' depth chart lists Fernando Mendoza as QB2
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has declined to say whether rookie Fernando Mendoza or Aidan O’Connell will back up starting quarterback Kirk Cousins.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has declined to say whether rookie Fernando Mendoza or Aidan O’Connell will back up starting quarterback Kirk Cousins. But the team's depth chart says it's Mendoza.

The Raiders released their first depth chart of the regular season today, and it has Mendoza as QB2 and O'Connell as QB3.

The first overall pick in the draft usually starts from Week 1 of his rookie year, but in Mendoza's case the Raiders are planning to bring him along slowly and let him learn behind Cousins. If Cousins goes down, however, it appears that Mendoza will be the next man up.

The Raiders are 3.5-point favorites at home against the Dolphins in Sunday's opener.

item.title: Baker Mayfield agrees to three-year extension with Buccaneers
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Mayfield's deal is reportedly worth $165 million.
item.content:encoded:
Apparently, Baker Mayfield is no longer feeling disrespected.

According to a joint report from NFL Network and ESPN, Mayfield and the Buccaneers have agreed to a three-year extension, putting him under contract through the 2029 season.

The deal is reportedly worth $165 million, which works out to $55 million a year.

Mayfield had cut off extension talks at the beginning of training camp, telling reporters at the time that he had felt disrespected by the Bucs' offer to him. But he also kept the door open to his agent potentially still talking numbers with the team.

As Mike Garafolo of NFL Network notes, the two sides were not that far apart at the start of training camp. Both sides came back to the negotiating table after a break and were able to get the deal done, preventing Mayfield from playing out a contract year.

Mayfield, the No. 1 overall pick of the 2018 draft, has been Tampa Bay's starter for the last three seasons. He initially signed with the club on a one-year deal, leading the Bucs to a division title and a postseason win in his first year. The Bucs went 10-7 in 2024 and won the NFC South before falling in the Wild Card round.

While the club started hot in 2025, Tampa Bay finished 8-9, missing the postseason.

Mayfield completed 63.2 percent of his passes last season for 3,693 yards with 25 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

The Buccaneers will begin the 2026 season on the road on Sunday against the Bengals.

item.title: Jayden Daniels among 5 Commanders captains
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The number five is important to Jayden Daniels, so perhaps it's appropriate that he's one of five captains on the Commanders this season.
item.content:encoded:
The number five is important to Jayden Daniels, so perhaps it's appropriate that he's one of five captains on the Commanders this season.

Washington announced that Daniels was chosen as a team captain alongside wide receiver Terry McLaurin, linebacker Frankie Luvu, safety Jeremy Reaves and punter Tress Way.

Daniels said he thinks being named a team captain is a natural extension of the leadership he exudes as the Commanders' starting quarterback.

"I just think it comes with reps here. Going into my third camp, my third year, I have more of a voice and you mature more over the years," Daniels said. "You play a lot of ball. You go do a lot of different things on and off the field, so you're gonna mature in this league. So now it's kind of just being more intentional with not only myself but getting the guys around me ready and rallying the troops."

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn has previously named weekly captains for the team rather than letting the players elect season-long captains, but he said this year that's one of the things he'd like to change, as he wanted the team to vote for players who represent the standards the Commanders want to set.
